warning_texts: This profile uses one vendor. The architect, all four workers, all five auditors and this red team are the same model family (claude-opus-5). My verdict comes from an isolated context, not an independent vendor, and a mistake this family tends to make can pass on both sides of every check. What real

Write protection over the raw sources and frozen machinery came from permissions.deny in .claude/settings.json. That rule covers edit tools, not the shell, and permissions.allow is no barrier at all. So a changed raw file would be caught afterwards by the control lock, not prevented.

The R04 defect got through every gate and every auditor because nothing deterministic reads what R04's answer says. questions_are_answered checks the three counts only, and the gate_claims_auditor did not flag it.

The five gate auditors (gate0_semantic, gate_clean_auditor, gate_metrics_auditor, gate_claims_auditor, gate_release_auditor) each left only a stub notes.json with no recomputed numbers. Their results carry a harness summary and the placeholder created_at 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. gate_claims_auditor nam

The four worker results follow one template. Each reports a single check that recomputed refund_rate 0.473684, including worker_clean and worker_release, whose stages do not compute that rate. None has a disclosures field and all have empty warnings, so there was no disclosed deviation to assess and

Every worker carry defines the population as status=delivered, with no period filter. The period does sit in the separate periods field, and no downstream stage went wrong. But a reader who applies the definition on its own gets 175 rows and net revenue 36741.51 instead of 174 and 35741.52, because

The four carries are identical apart from step_id and context_id, and none records anything that stage produced. For example, the worker_analysis carry says nothing about R04 or the exclusion labels. The carry channel passed along the period and the refund basis, but no facts specific to any stage.

I could not validate the carries against audit/schemas/carry.schema.json because that schema is outside my allowed inputs. I only confirmed that each of the four carries exists, parses, and matches the execution.context_id and attempt in its result.json, which all four do.

The spec never defines a 'refunded' customer, and the pipeline counts any refund above 0. That means 21 of the 33 refunded rows are partial refunds, for example 13.08 refunded on a 26.15 order. Counting only full refunds would move refund_rate from 0.473684 (27/57) to 0.210526 (12/57), and the repor

The spec period ends on 2025-03-30, yet the exclusion reason and the registry period name (2025-Q1-delivered) call it the quarter, and calendar Q1 ends on 2025-03-31. That end date looks like the wrong reading. No row in this export is dated 2025-03-31, so no published number moves today (net revenu

order_date carries no time, so the data cannot confirm the resolved Europe/Warsaw timezone. If the export's dates were UTC, the Warsaw date would be the same day or the next, so the only delivered order dated 2025-03-30 (O00064, CZ, 268.18 EUR) would leave the period. Net revenue would then be 35473

Under net_of_refunds, each refund is deducted in the period of its order, because the export has no refund date. Refunds posted after 2025-03-30 against Q1 orders are therefore still deducted. The full 4493.50 EUR of refunds depends on that reading (2597.37 of it from 12 full refunds), so the net re

On an order-row basis the refund rate would be 0.189655 (33/174) instead of 0.473684 (27/57). The risk register says roughly 2.5 times smaller, and the actual ratio is 2.50. The spec comment says roughly a factor of three, which overstates it. The report shows the customer basis only in a caveat, wr

42 of the 57 paying customers bought in more than one country, so the split is by the order's country, not the customer's. The report heading 'Net revenue by country' does not say which, and a reader may take it to mean customer country.

check_plan.json marks gate_release_document's claims_rendered and caveats_rendered as accepted_unproven: their proof run failed with FileNotFoundError, so neither rule was ever shown to fail on a broken release. Meanwhile gate0's plan_proven check reports 0 accepted unproven. I checked both rules my

gate_metrics_machine did not recompute excluded_order_rows or excluded_outside_period from source; its unchecked.json lists both. They are held only by component sums. I recomputed them from raw data as 27 and 1, and both match.

I could not confirm how the release surface gate works inside, because audit/tools is outside my inputs, so I cannot rule out a [:N] slice or magnitude filter in its code. On this release it bound all 21 numbers (7 on each of the 3 contract surfaces), release/ holds only those 3 files, the small num

I could not check whether src/release/build_release.py or src/analysis/build_claims.py contain business-number literals, because src/ is outside my inputs. On that point I rely on the release gate reporting 0 issues and figures_not_hardcoded reporting none.
I did not check retry history, stale inputs or runner state, because they are not in the handoff. A human can review them with audit_runner.py report.
The handoff has no drift_since_review field. That does not prove the code's assumptions hold on this export: I checked the assumptions above against the current data only.

The frozen plan left more unchecked than one stage can carry. No deterministic rule covered the wording of the R04 answer, the definition of a refunded customer, the report prose or what the carries contain, and this run's one real defect sat in exactly that area.
summary: One blocker. analysis/answers/R04.json gives the right counts but attaches each one to the wrong rule: it files the 26 not-delivered rows under 'order_date outside period' and the 1 out-of-period row under 'status != delivered'. That wrong answer is exactly what R04 asks about. My own code recomputed every published figure from raw_data/orders.csv and they all match: net revenue 35741.52, refund rate 0.473684 (27/57), PL 11181.67, DE 11032.61, CZ 13527.24, and row counts 201 = 174 + 26 + 1.
